description: This bar chart, from the paper “2-Tier SimCSE Elevating BERT for Robust Sentence Embeddings,” compares the performance of five different models across three metrics: Sentiment Accuracy (light yellow), STS Correlation (pink), and Paraphrase Accuracy (light blue). The horizontal axis lists the models in order from left to right: Single-task_baseline, Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout, Unsupervised_SimCSE, Supervised_SimCSE, and 2-Tier SimCSE. The vertical axis, labeled “Accuracy / Correlation,” ranges from 0 to 0.8 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. For each model, three bars are grouped together, representing its performance on each of the three tasks. The Single-task_baseline model shows the lowest performance, with Sentiment Acc. at approximately 0.53, STS Corr. at approximately 0.50, and Paraphrase Acc. at approximately 0.79. The Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout shows a slight improvement, with Sentiment Acc. at approximately 0.52, STS Corr. at approximately 0.58, and Paraphrase Acc. at approximately 0.78. The Unsupervised_SimCSE model shows a notable increase in STS Corr. to approximately 0.70, while Sentiment Acc. remains around 0.52 and Paraphrase Acc. is approximately 0.77. The Supervised_SimCSE model achieves the highest STS Corr. at approximately 0.81 and Paraphrase Acc. at approximately 0.78, with Sentiment Acc. at approximately 0.48. The 2-Tier SimCSE model, the final model shown, achieves the highest overall performance, with STS Corr. at approximately 0.81 and Paraphrase Acc. at approximately 0.78, while Sentiment Acc. is approximately 0.49. The bars are not sorted, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color-coding as defined in the legend.
